channel.title: Sneaky Deals facebook queue
channel.description: Approved videos for the Sneaky Deals Facebook Page. Zap "Sneaky Deals -> Facebook" (RSS by Zapier -> Facebook Pages Create Page Video) reads this feed. n8n adds one item per publish day, right after feed/youtube.xml.

item.title: Domino's 30-Minute Promise Ended by a Jury
item.description:
Domino's promised pizza in 30 minutes or free, until a 1993 jury award of over $78 million. Days later the guarantee was gone. Would you have used it? 👇
#dominos #businesshistory

item.title: Nike Paid $35 for Its Swoosh Logo
item.description:
In 1971 a Portland State design student invoiced Nike's founder $35 for the Swoosh. He said he didn't love it, but it would grow on him. In 1983 Nike gave her a gold Swoosh ring and stock. Would you have charged more? 👇
#nike #businesshistory

item.title: Costco's $1.50 Hot Dog Hasn't Changed Price Since 1985
item.description:
Costco's hot dog and soda combo has cost $1.50 since 1985. When it was losing money, Costco built its own hot dog factories rather than raise the price. Would you still shop there at $4? 👇
#costco #businesshistory

item.title: Taco John's Owned 'Taco Tuesday' Until Taco Bell Stepped In
item.description:
A small Wyoming chain trademarked "Taco Tuesday" in 1989. In 2023 Taco Bell asked the government to cancel it, and Taco John's gave it up.
What's your Taco Tuesday order? 👇
#tacotuesday #businesshistory

item.title: Coca-Cola Gave Away Millions of Free Drinks on Purpose
item.description:
In 1887 Asa Candler gave out handwritten tickets for one free glass of Coke. Roughly 8.5 million free drinks later, it was served in every state, and Coca-Cola is widely considered the first company to offer coupons.
Would you have taken the ticket? 👇
#cocacola #businesshistory

item.title: McDonald's Monopoly Was Rigged by Its Own Security Chief
item.description:
The man guarding the game's winning pieces secretly gave them to friends and family, who posed as winners and paid him a cut. The FBI's Operation Final Answer ended it in 2001.
Did you ever play? 👇
#mcdonalds #businesshistory

item.title: Wrigley Mailed Free Gum to a Million Strangers in 1915
item.description:
Before gum, Wrigley sold soap, then baking powder — each time giving away the next product free until it outsold the last. In 1915 he mailed free gum to about 1.5 million US homes from the phone book.
Genius or wasteful? 👇
#wrigley #businesshistory

item.title: Hoover Offered Free Flights With Vacuums and It Cost Millions
item.description:
In 1992 Hoover's British branch offered two free return flights for spending £100. It expected about 50,000 claims; hundreds of thousands came, and Maytag later sold the European business.
Would you have bought the vacuum? 👇
#hoover #businesshistory

item.title: Pepsi's Ad Showed a Fighter Jet, So a Student Sent a $700,000 Check
item.description:
In 1996 a Pepsi ad showed a Harrier jet for 7,000,000 Pepsi Points. Points cost 10 cents each, so a student raised $700,000 and mailed Pepsi a check. Pepsi said it was a joke, and in 1999 a judge agreed.
Should Pepsi have handed over the jet? 👇
#pepsi #businesshistory

item.title: Piggly Wiggly's Founder Bet $10 Million Against Wall Street
item.description:
In 1916 Clarence Saunders invented self-service grocery shopping. Years later he borrowed about $10 million to beat the traders betting against his stock. The price hit $124 by noon, then the stock exchange stopped trading and he went bankrupt.
Robbed, or pushed too far? 👇
#pigglywiggly #businesshistory

item.title: This Man Turned $3,000 of Pudding Into 1.2 Million Airline Miles
item.description:
In 1999, David Phillips noticed a Healthy Choice promo paid airline miles for barcodes, and pudding cost about 25 cents a cup. He bought 12,150 cups and earned more than 1.2 million miles.
Genius loophole or too far? 👇
#puddingguy #businesshistory

item.title: Disney Secretly Bought a Swamp Using Fake Names
item.description:
Walt Disney hid behind fake companies (one was called "M.T. Lott") to buy 27,000+ acres of Florida swamp for under $200 an acre, before a reporter cracked the secret in 1965.
Was it smart business or a dirty trick? 👇
#disney #businesshistory
